title: Hanukkah Lights
strapline: One more candle lit each night for eight nights, spinning dreidels, and the warm glow of the menorah in the winter dark.
intent: Hanukkah, the Jewish festival of lights, celebrates hope and a small light lasting far longer than anyone expected, over eight nights of growing brightness — a gentle, warm theme for the darkest time of year.
Honouring a real celebration from families in the community helps every child value their friends' traditions and feel proud when their own are shared.
Making menorahs, playing with dreidels and creating light-themed crafts invites lovely creative and fine-motor work.
The festival is full of number — eight nights and one more candle each evening, the four-sided dreidel, counting and matching in the games.
Children grow knowledge of the wider world and language to talk about it — candle, light, eight, spin, celebrate, festival, hope.
Lighting the candles together, playing the dreidel game and sharing special foods builds turn-taking, patience and joyful community.
implementation: Learn about Hanukkah with families who celebrate it — invite them to share how they mark it, and follow their lead so it is accurate and respectful.
Offer menorah-making (with battery lights, never real flames), dreidel play, and crafts around light, stars and candles.
Model the counting and the wonder: 'Tonight there'd be three candles lit — one more than last night. Shall we count them together?'
Bring in maths through the traditions — add one candle each 'night', play the number-and-spin dreidel game, match and count as you go.
Play and celebrate together — the dreidel game with tokens to win and share, songs, and the growing row of lights night by night.
Where safe and with families, share special foods (like latkes), and make cards and decorations to give and display.
key_questions: Tonight there'd be three candles — one more than last night. Shall we count them?
How many nights does Hanukkah last?
Which way did the dreidel land — how many tokens do you win?
How does the row of lights change each night?
How does your family celebrate Hanukkah at home?

impact.text: Children value a real festival of light and hope and feel proud when their own traditions are shared.
Children make menorahs, play with dreidels and create light-themed crafts.
Children add one candle each night, count to eight and match and count in the dreidel game.
Children grow words for the festival — candle, light, eight, spin, celebrate, hope.
Children take turns, share and wait, building patience and joyful community.

enhancements: Menorah-making with battery lights, never real flames.
The dreidel game with tokens to win and share.
A growing row of lights added to night by night.
Latkes or other special foods shared where safe and with families.
Cards and light-themed decorations to give and display.

playing_exploring: Children explore light, spinning and counting through a warm real festival, bringing their own family experiences to it.
They make, decorate and play their way into the celebration.
active_learning: Children take turns and stay with the dreidel game and the nightly lighting, absorbed in the shared ritual.
creating_thinking: Children count and add the candles night by night and make sense of a festival alongside their own.
